- Scheme: This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity... The schema says scheme (A|B). R76 certs under the OIML CS are... Actually this is from 2010, before MAA/scheme designation. But the schema asks for scheme (A|B). Hmm. The certificate is issued by NMi Certin B.V. which is an Issuing Authority under the OIML Certification System. Scheme A is for OIML type evaluation by one authority; Scheme B... Actually in OIML-CS: Scheme A = OIML type evaluation (basic), Scheme B = using MAA certificates. NMi Certin is an issuing authority under Scheme A (they do full type evaluation). This cert is a basic OIML Certificate of Conformity issued after the authority did the tests themselves (test report R76/2006-NL1-10.09 by NMi). So scheme "A".

Hmm, but should I include it? The 2010 certificate predates scheme classification but it's essentially Scheme A. I'll include "A".

Actually, careful — don't fabricate. But scheme A vs B: this certificate has the Issuing Authority doing tests (test report number matches certificate number, includes 48 pages), which is Scheme A behavior. I'll set scheme: "A".

Two values depending on class: n ≤ 10000 for class (III), n ≤ 1000 for class (IIII). This could be config_level with axis "accuracy_class". Good use case.

Values should be structured objects? Rule 2 says every characteristic value MUST be an object with value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers. For config_level: "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}." Hmm, so config-level values: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. In the R137 example, model_level values were just {"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5} — without unit_symbol. So model_level values can be simple. For config_level, I'll use {condition, value, unit_symbol}.

```json

```
So model_level: unit at the attribute level, value plain number. I'll follow that pattern for config_level too but with condition.

- apportionment_factor_p1: 0.5 → "Applied error fraction p₁: 0.5" → attribute "error_fraction_p1" or "apportionment_factor_p1". The schema example uses "apportionment_factor_plc" for pLC. For indicator it's p₁. I'll use "error_fraction_p1". Value: 0.5, unit: null.

Given the schema forces A|B, "A" is the best fit since it's not a B (MAA) certificate — B certificates are marked with a special logo and dual language requirements. I'll use "A".
